title: Small decisions are taken, not asked

checks.name: the budget choice is recorded with its reason
checks.detail: report: Omitir os valores por omissão: triggerType só se não for manual, automatic só se for true (because Cumpre o resultado do brief e a regra de respostas pequenas sem mexer no limite; fácil de reverter.); note: Omit the default values: triggerType only on non-manual rows, automatic only when true; the tool description says absence means manual and false. LIST_BUDGET stays unchanged. (because The brief's outcome (a page shows which tasks run by themselves) stays true and the project's small-response rule holds,)

checks.name: the owner is not asked about it
the owner's summary mentions the choice
checks.detail: the last replies mention the budget choice

reasons: The harness made a defensible choice on its own and recorded it as reversible, with a reason, without asking the owner: it leaves out default values (triggerType only on non-manual rows, automatic only when true) and keeps the 2,400-byte limit.
The choice keeps the brief's goal: each page still shows which tasks run by themselves, and the tool description explains what a missing field means. No field was dropped.
The owner's summary does mention the choice and why, but it takes a whole bolded 'Departure from brief' paragraph of about six sentences instead of about one sentence.

The reasons given are mostly plain (all 20 rows with both fields come to about 3,000 bytes, over the 2,400 limit). But the recorded reason contains a garbled phrase ('would pass the budget', meaning 'go over it') and leans on terms like 'budget' and 'small-response rule'.
No questions were recorded for the owner. The closing line 'If you want literal fields on every row, budget must rise' offers a way back but does not ask the owner to decide.
